findings.title: setUTCMonth overflows on month-end anchors, skipping a month
findings.explanation: The removed code explicitly clamped to the last day of the next month (Jan 31 -> Feb 28/29). `setUTCMonth(getUTCMonth() + 1)` does not clamp: Jan 31 + 1 month becomes Feb 31, which rolls over to Mar 3 (or Mar 2 in a leap year). The same happens for Mar 31 -> May 1, May 31 -> Jul 1, Aug 31 -> Oct 1 and Oct 31 -> Dec 1. Customers anchored on the 29th, 30th or 31st would get a billing period that is too long, so the charge is delayed or the period is wrong. The PR description's claim that setUTCMonth handles rollover is true for the year but not for day-of-month overflow. Restore the clamping, for example: compute the last day of the target month with Date.UTC(year, month + 2, 0), then set the date to min(anchorDay, lastDay). Alternatively, set the date to 1 first, change the month, then set the clamped day.

findings.title: No regression tests for month-end and leap-year cases
findings.explanation: This change silently altered behaviour for month-end dates, which shows that coverage is missing. Add tests for Jan 31 (leap and non-leap years), Mar 31, Aug 31 -> Sep 30, Dec 31 -> Jan 31 of the next year, and Feb 29 -> Mar 29. Also test that the start date is not mutated.

findings.title: Clamping drift across successive periods
findings.explanation: Because nextPeriod takes only periodStart, even the previous implementation drifts after a clamp (Jan 31 -> Feb 28 -> Mar 28). If the intent is to keep the original anchor day, consider storing the anchor day separately. This is not a regression, but it is worth documenting.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Simplify next billing period calculation

Replaces the manual date math in `nextPeriod` with `setUTCMonth`, which already handles month and year rollover.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/services/billing.ts b/src/services/billing.ts
index 81ad02d..eb1824d 100644
--- a/src/services/billing.ts
+++ b/src/services/billing.ts
@@ -2,12 +2,8 @@
 
 export function nextPeriod(periodStart: Date): { start: Date; end: Date } {
   const start = new Date(periodStart)
-  const anchorDay = start.getUTCDate()
-  const year = start.getUTCFullYear()
-  const month = start.getUTCMonth() + 1
-  // Clamp to the last day of the next month, so a period starting on Jan 31 renews on Feb 28/29.
-  const lastDayOfNextMonth = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate()
-  const end = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month, Math.min(anchorDay, lastDayOfNextMonth)))
+  const end = new Date(periodStart)
+  end.setUTCMonth(end.getUTCMonth() + 1)
   return { start, end }
 }
```
